chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Ammar ibn Marwan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام): “My father was overtaken by death, so I said to him, ‘Make a will.’ He said, ‘This is my son’—meaning Umar—‘whatever he does is valid.’” So Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) said: “Your father has indeed made a will, and he was concise.”
He said: I said, “He instructed and made a bequest for you of such-and-such.” He said: “Approve it.”

I said: “He made a bequest for a believing, knowledgeable slave, but when we emancipated her, it became clear that she was not of proper lineage.” He said: “It has sufficed for him. The likeness of that is only like a man who bought a sacrificial animal thinking it was fat, then found it thin; it has still sufficed for him.”

key_terms.أَجِزْ: approve it and allow it to stand
key_terms.أَوْصَى: he made a will or bequest
key_terms.نَسَمَةٍ: a human slave person to be emancipated

ai.seo_question: Does a bequest remain valid if a hidden defect is discovered after carrying it out?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses rulings related to wills and the validity of broadly delegated authority in carrying out a dying person's testament. It also establishes that when a bequest is fulfilled according to apparent qualification, later discovery of a hidden deficiency does not invalidate the act, as illustrated by the analogy of a sacrificial animal thought to be fat but found thin.
